verdict_reasoning: The goal has shown demand and no objection at level 1 survived. The listener design is not settled: message #52 questions the single-port proxy_networks shape and message #53 only plans a rework (prior-attempts-1, standards-compat-1). Trust for Unix-domain sockets (security-1) and the header-supplied raddr (maintenance-fit-2) also need answers in the design. Code review makes sense once the list agrees on the configuration shape.

brief.title: PROXY protocol support for client addresses behind proxies
brief.problem: When Postgres runs behind a load balancer or proxy such as HAProxy, Envoy or a cloud load balancer, the server sees the proxy's address instead of the client's. So pg_hba.conf rules, log lines and pg_stat_activity use the wrong address, which matters for audit and conformance requirements.
brief.proposed_design: The server accepts the PROXY protocol header, a one-way prefix before the normal startup packet, from trusted proxies and uses the address in it as the client address. Magnus Hagander's patches (v1 to v11) used a separate proxy_port plus a proxy_servers trust list. Julien Riou's rewrite (v12, v13) uses one port and a proxy_networks list, supports protocol v1 and v2, and in message #53 he considers going back to a per-listener port with a trust list.
user_visible_surface: GUC proxy_servers (v1 to v11): list of trusted proxy IPs, CIDRs or the literal unix.
GUC proxy_port (v3 to v11): separate TCP port that accepts only PROXY connections.
GUC proxy_networks (v12, v13): trusted networks on the regular port; a connection from them without a header is rejected.
pg_stat_activity columns for the proxy address, hostname and port, plus proxy fields in stderr, csvlog and jsonlog (v12).
inet_server_addr() and inet_server_port() return the address and port the client used to reach the proxy; ident auth is disabled for proxied connections.
author_claims: The PROXY protocol is a light, widely used standard, supported by HAProxy, Envoy and cloud load balancers.
A single port is simpler for operators because existing network rules keep working (Riou).
Late parsing means no performance regression unless proxy_networks is set; no numbers are given.
An untrusted client that omits the header gets the generic incomplete startup packet error, so scanners cannot detect the feature.
The TAP suite in src/test/protocol covers the changes; the reviewer reports 71 passing tests.
brief.thread_state: Peter Eisentraut questioned the single-port proxy_networks design and suggested a general endpoint list setting; Riou surveyed other products and plans to rework toward a per-listener port with a trust list. Manu reported v12 testing results and asked whether the connection received log line should show the client address.
unclear: The material does not say which configuration design the next version will use, or whether listen_addresses-style endpoint syntax is in scope.
No v14 patch prose is shown, so docs for proxy_networks and the new pg_stat_activity columns cannot be checked.
The material does not say how multiple Unix-domain sockets are each marked as proxy or not.
No benchmark backs the claim of no connection-time regression.
The proposal does not say whether connection received logs the proxy or the client address.

objections.title: Trusting Unix sockets lets any local OS user claim any client IP
objections.failure_scenario: An admin trusts Unix sockets so that a sidecar Envoy can forward connections. Another OS user on the same host, such as an application account, connects to the same socket with a forged header and claims an address that matches a `host ... trust` or weaker pg_hba line. pg_hba accepts the forged address, and the logs record it as the real client.
objections.argument: Message #34 notes that the PROXY socket cannot get its own permissions, so local access to the main socket becomes the power to set the source address. Message #52 notes that all Unix-domain sockets are trusted or none are. Both points were deferred to a later version in messages #41 and #42, and v12 and v13 do not change them. Under this design the trust boundary for a pg_hba bypass is whoever may open the socket file, which nothing in the documentation hunks warns about.
objections.author_must_show: How does the next version make sure that only the intended proxy, and not every OS user who can open the socket, can send a trusted PROXY header over a Unix socket?

critic.reasoning: Message #34 names unix_socket_group and unix_socket_permissions as the only control, and they cannot be set separately for the PROXY socket. Messages #41 and #42 deferred this, and message #52 confirms v12 treats all Unix-domain sockets alike.

objections.title: Single-port design reopens the port-sharing issue the spec warns about
objections.failure_scenario: An operator puts a load balancer subnet into proxy_networks on a host that also has a monitoring agent or a second, non-PROXY proxy on that subnet. Every header-less connection from that subnet is rejected. The operator finds out at the next deploy, when health checks or tools fail, and the only fix is another IP address.
objections.argument: Message #3 quotes the spec text that "explicitly prevents port sharing", and messages #4, #9 and #12 moved Magnus's patches to a separate proxy_port for that reason. The v12 rewrite returns to one port and makes trust depend on source address only. Message #52 says this ties a host to the PROXY protocol, invites IPv4/IPv6 confusion, and does not handle more than one Unix-domain socket. Message #53 says the author is only considering a return to a per-listener design, so the current patch still carries the issue.
objections.author_must_show: Will v14 mark individual listeners, Unix-domain sockets included, as PROXY-only, and how does it then handle mixed PROXY and plain clients from one trusted network?

critic.reasoning: Message #52 raises the same points against v12 and v13, and message #53 only says the author is considering a per-listener rework. No posted version answers it yet, so it stands as fixable.

objections.title: Listener configuration is unsettled and any new GUC may become permanent
objections.failure_scenario: Version 20 ships proxy_port or proxy_networks, and operators build configurations and automation around it. A later release adds the endpoint list from message #52 for direct SSL and other listener properties. The project then keeps two overlapping ways to mark a listener as PROXY, with rules for which one wins, for many years.
objections.argument: The thread has used three shapes: proxy_servers only, proxy_port plus proxy_servers, and proxy_networks on the shared port. In message #52 a committer prefers a general endpoint facility because each per-feature GUC covers only one slice, and message #53 plans to return to a separate port. Message #52 also notes that several Unix-domain sockets cannot be marked one by one under the single literal unix. A GUC cannot be removed without breaking configurations, so the shape should be chosen before the first one ships.
objections.author_must_show: How would the chosen PROXY setting fit a later general endpoint list, including separate Unix-domain sockets, without leaving a duplicate GUC to deprecate?

critic.reasoning: A committer asked in message #52 how the setting relates to a general endpoint list. Message #53 picks a narrower shape without saying how it would fit one later, so the question is open.

objections.title: Proxied raddr becomes an invariant that future auth code must remember
objections.failure_scenario: A later patch adds an authentication method or a check that trusts port->raddr as the real TCP peer, as ident does. On proxied connections the address comes from the header instead, and the new code makes a trust decision on it. No test or assertion catches this, so the problem shows up in production.
objections.argument: Message #25 shows that raddr no longer matches a real connection to laddr. It names ident as one case that breaks. Message #26 adds SSL and GSSAPI checks that also had to change. Message #41 says only ident was found, after a manual search of the auth code. The proposal does not say what tells a future author that raddr may be synthetic.
objections.author_must_show: What makes a future auth method or connection check fail loudly, or at least warn the author, if it treats a header-supplied raddr as the real peer?

critic.reasoning: Message #41 says the search for raddr users besides ident was manual and incomplete, and message #42 agrees it needs more review. The v12 rewrite does not say what marks a header-supplied address for later auth code.

objections.title: Log lines show two different client addresses for one connection
objections.failure_scenario: An operator turns on PROXY support and keeps log_connections enabled. The 'connection received' line logs the proxy address, while the authentication line and pg_stat_activity use the client address from the header. Log parsers and ban tools that read source addresses from 'connection received' then attribute every connection to the proxy, and nobody notices until an audit.
objections.argument: Message #51 shows this behaviour in v12 and asks for one of two fixes, but the thread has not chosen. The stated purpose of the feature is correct addresses in logs for audit, per messages #1 and #6, so a first log line with the proxy address works against the purpose. The meaning of an existing log line for proxied connections is part of the user-facing contract and should be fixed in the design.
objections.author_must_show: For a proxied connection, which address will 'connection received' report, and where is the other address logged?

critic.reasoning: Message #51 shows the two addresses in consecutive log lines and offers two fixes. Message #53 does not pick one, and correct addresses in logs are the stated purpose in messages #1 and #6.

refuted.title: New proxy columns in pg_stat_activity may expose internal addresses
refuted.failure_scenario: Under v12, an unprivileged role queries pg_stat_activity and reads proxy_addr, the proxy host name and proxy_port for other sessions. That role learns the internal addresses of the load balancer tier, which the change to inet_server_addr() was meant to hide.
refuted.argument: Message #32 changed inet_server_addr() so that the server does not expose network internals to clients. Message #34 suggested that any way to see the proxy-side address be limited to pg_monitor-level roles. Message #49 adds proxy_addr, the proxy host name and proxy_port to pg_stat_activity but does not say whether they get the same per-role masking as client_addr. If they are not masked, the patch brings back the disclosure that message #32 removed.
refuted.author_must_show: Are the new proxy columns in pg_stat_activity hidden from roles that lack pg_read_all_stats, in the same way as client_addr?

critic.reasoning: The scenario assumes the new columns are visible to unprivileged roles, which the material does not show. pg_stat_activity already hides client_addr of other sessions from roles without pg_read_all_stats, and only the code can show whether the new columns differ.

refuted.title: Single-purpose listener settings before a general endpoint syntax exists
refuted.failure_scenario: Release N ships proxy_port, or proxy_networks, with its own trust list. A later release adds per-endpoint properties for direct SSL or for Unix sockets. The project then either keeps two ways to say which listener speaks PROXY, or breaks existing postgresql.conf files that use the old setting.
refuted.argument: In message #52 Peter Eisentraut asks for a general way to list socket endpoints, with parallel settings for proxy, direct-SSL and other endpoints. He says any narrower setting covers only one slice of the cases. Message #53 plans to return to a per-listener port plus a trust list because it is the smallest change, which is the narrow slice. The thread does not show how that setting would map onto a later endpoint list.
refuted.author_must_show: How would the planned proxy port and trust list settings map onto a later listen_addresses-style endpoint list without a second, overlapping configuration path?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1, which makes the same point about a later endpoint list and also covers separate Unix-domain sockets.

touch_points.label: wire protocol
touch_points.reason: The server reads a PROXY header before the normal startup packet on a connection.

touch_points.label: catalog changes
touch_points.reason: v12 adds proxy address, host name and port columns to the pg_stat_activity system view.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: The patch changes libpq-be.h and libpq.h, and makes raddr a header-supplied address that extensions may read.

touch_points.label: new GUC
touch_points.reason: The versions add proxy_servers, proxy_port or proxy_networks, and the final shape is not chosen.

touch_points.label: security / privileges
touch_points.reason: pg_hba.conf matching uses an address taken from a header sent by a trusted proxy; ident is disabled for proxied connections.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: New listener settings, new log and view fields, and a rule that later auth code must not treat raddr as the real peer.

touch_points.label: performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: The patch changes connection startup in postmaster.c and pqcomm.c; no benchmark backs the no-regression claim.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Which configuration will v14 use: a per-listener PROXY port with a trust list, the shared port with proxy_networks, or a general endpoint list as suggested in message #52?
How does the next version stop every OS user who can open a trusted Unix-domain socket from sending a PROXY header with a forged client address?
How would the chosen PROXY setting fit a later general endpoint list, including separate Unix-domain sockets, without leaving a duplicate GUC to deprecate?
What makes a future authentication method or connection check fail loudly if it treats a header-supplied raddr as the real TCP peer?
For a proxied connection, which address does the "connection received" log line report, and where is the other address logged?

committability.owner_note: Peter Eisentraut commented on the listener design in message #52. The owner needs to know postmaster connection startup, pg_hba.conf matching and the authentication code.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a pg_hba.conf trust decision based on a proxy-supplied address, for new listener GUCs that cannot be removed later, and for every later auth change that reads raddr. This lasts as long as the feature exists.
committability.author_follow_up: The current author posted v12 and v13, and in message #53 answered the design review with a survey and a rework plan. The entry is tagged as a first patch, and the original author's versions stopped at v11.

priority.reason: Independent users asked for this from 2021 to 2026, and the feature is off by default. The listener configuration and the Unix-domain socket trust rule are open after message #52, so a v14 that settles them should come before detailed review of postmaster and auth changes.

provisional_note: Only patch prose for v1 and v11 was read; no v12 or v13 prose is shown. The masking of the new pg_stat_activity columns, the full set of raddr users and the connection-time cost can only be checked in the code.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Built-in connection proxy
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a built-in connection proxy: clients connect to a separate port (6543 by default), and proxy workers spread their sessions over a small pool of backends. A backend whose session changes state (GUCs, temporary tables, prepared statements) is marked tainted and stays dedicated to that client.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier marked the entry Returned with Feedback because the patch needed another rebase and had been Waiting on Author for six weeks. The author had posted a rebased patch on 2020-07-02 but did not change the status, and he did not notice it stopped applying. Earlier reviews raised open design issues: pool limits that are per proxy and not global, too little monitoring, coarse tainting, and a busy loop with poll().
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This needs again a rebase, and has been waiting on author for 6 weeks
now, so I am switching it to RwF.

precedents_retrieved.title: Respect client-initiated CopyDone during logical streaming replication
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes the walsender honor a client-initiated CopyDone during logical streaming, both while waiting for WAL and while ReorderBufferCommit sends a large transaction, so a client can return to command mode without closing the connection. Later versions added a continue_decoding_cb callback in the reorder buffer and taught pg_recvlogical to send CopyDone on SIGINT, with TAP tests.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund objected to adding another callback and suggested raising an error in the prepare write callback, since a partial transaction may already have been sent when decoding stops. The author asked how this should work for output plugins that send only at commit, and the reviewers did not follow up. No updated patch appears, and the entry was marked returned with feedback; the visible messages do not show the final withdrawal.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I don't think it's a good idea to return a non-error state if a command is interrupted in the middle. We might already have sent a partial transaction or such.

precedents_retrieved.title: Implement NULL-related checks in object address functions to prevent cache lookup errors
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch set makes the SQL functions pg_describe_object, pg_identify_object and pg_identify_object_as_address return NULL for undefined objects instead of raising "cache lookup failed" errors. It adds missing_ok flags to getObjectDescription, getObjectIdentity and lower-level lookup routines such as get_attname, GetForeignServer and the publication and subscription lookups.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Several preparatory patches were committed during the thread, but the main objectaddress patch was not. In its last review, Alvaro Herrera found that pg_identify_object returned an empty type in only some cases, and that it reported a column for a relation with no such column. The author fixed the column case, but left open whether type, operator and function formatting should be reworked to return NULL for undefined objects. The visible messages show no reply after that, and no closing message.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: One thing is that I am not sure if it is worth complicating the existing interface even more just to deal with undefined objects as pure NULLs.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert my bad decision of about a year ago to make PortalDefineQuery responsible for copying the query string into the new Portal.
precedents_retrieved.summary: Revert my bad decision of about a year ago to make PortalDefineQuery responsible for copying the query string into the new Portal.  Such copying is unnecessary in the common code path through exec_simple_query, and in this case it can be enormously expensive because the string might contain a large number of individual commands; we were copying the entire, long string for each command, resulting in O(N^2) behavior for N commands. (This is the cause of bug #4079.)  A second problem with it is that PortalDefineQuery really can't risk error, because if it elog's before having set up the Portal, we will leak the plancache refcount that the caller is trying to hand off to the portal.  So go back to the design in which the caller is responsible for making sure everything is copied into the portal if necessary.

precedents_retrieved.summary:
Embedded server
Section: Features We Do Not Want
precedents_retrieved.objection: While PostgreSQL clients runs fine in limited-resource environments, the server requires multiple processes and a stable pool of resources to run reliably and efficiently. Stripping down the PostgreSQL server to run in the same process address space as the client application would add too much complexity and failure cases. Besides, there are several very mature embedded SQL databases already available.

It lets users check pg_hba.conf before a reload and shows each rule's options in a jsonb column, built with new helper functions such as push_jsonb_string_value().

precedents_retrieved.title: "Causal reads" mode for load balancing reads without stale data
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch series adds a causal_reads mode: the primary tracks apply lag on each standby, and a commit waits until every standby still available for causal reads has applied it. A standby whose authorization has expired raises an error instead of returning stale data, and pg_stat_replication shows which standbys are available.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Only the first patch, synchronous_commit = remote_apply, was committed for 9.6. Robert Haas found that the replay lag patch puts a loop inside a spinlock-protected critical section and lacks comments and an overview of the mechanism. The later causal reads patches had little review, so the author said he could not post a tested fix before the feature freeze and the entry was returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Well, one problem with this is that you can't put a loop inside of a
spinlock-protected critical section.

precedents_retrieved.title: SERIALIZABLE on standby servers
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch allows SERIALIZABLE READ ONLY DEFERRABLE transactions on standby servers by having the primary write snapshot safety information into commit records and separate WAL records. The standby waits for a point in the WAL stream where a snapshot is known to be safe, using hypothetical transactions that the primary tracks as stand-ins for standby transactions.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author called the patch prototype/WIP code with unsolved problems. Two of them are a race between the safety decision and the order of commit records in WAL, and the absence of snapshot safety information in checkpoints. A third is that the primary makes transactions visible in ProcArrayEndTransaction() order while the standby uses commit record order, which can allow serialization anomalies. No review of the general approach came, and the entry was later withdrawn; the visible messages do not show who withdrew it.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: And that's precisely the issue: on the primary, transactions become visible to other transactions in the order in which they perform ProcArrayEndTransaction(), but on the standby, they become visible in the order in which they RecordTransactionCommit().

precedents_retrieved.title: "synchronous_replay" mode for load balancing reads without stale data
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a synchronous_replay mode (first called causal reads), in which the primary sends time-limited read leases to standbys whose replay lag stays under synchronous_replay_max_lag. With the mode on, a transaction on a standby sees all earlier synchronous_replay commits or gets an error, so read-only queries can be load balanced across replicas without stale data.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Dmitry Dolgov's testing with installcheck and pgbench crashed replicas with errors in WAL redo and the WAL stream. The author reproduced the problem on another machine but posted no fix before the commitfest ended, so Michael Paquier marked the entry returned with feedback. Simon Riggs's earlier design doubts appear only in quoted fragments, so they may have played a part, but the visible messages do not show them deciding it.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Yeah, it looks like the patch may be corrupting the WAL stream in some case that I didn't hit in my own testing procedure.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found in the list. The earlier attempt is Magnus Hagander's v1 to v11 in this thread. It stalled on rebase, not on rejection (messages #46 to #48), and its separate-port design is what the author plans to return to in message #53.
Behaviour changes for existing users happen only when the feature is configured. The retrieval found no relevant precedent.

From this angle the proposal has no on-disk, WAL, replication-slot or catalog-table state, and adds no new protocol message: the PROXY header is a pre-startup prefix, and existing clients and libpq do not change. The new pg_stat_activity columns and csvlog/jsonlog fields follow how earlier releases added columns there, and the next version's listener design is not yet written, so it could not be checked.

Message #51 settled DoS from truncated headers, since authentication_timeout covers it, and scanner detection. A broad proxy_networks CIDR is a trust risk, but message #53 moves back to a per-listener port that a firewall can restrict.

The connection-time cost is limited to connections that start up, and the feature is opt-in, so I raise no hot-path objection. A benchmark is still missing. Ownership is a committability matter. The original committer-author has been inactive since 2022, and the current author is new.

Postgres has no existing feature, GUC, hook or contrib module that recovers the client address from a proxy, and the header has to be read in the postmaster before authentication, which an extension cannot reach today. Network-level transparent proxying keeps the client IP, but it needs kernel and routing changes and is not available with many load balancers, so it does not cover the same need.

The material shows real and lasting demand from independent users, including audit-driven HAProxy use (message #6), Envoy sidecar production use (message #24) and requests from 2021 to 2026 (messages #48, #49, #51). Message #53 lists more than fifteen other products that support the protocol, and the feature is off by default, so its cost falls mostly on its users.
